title: C# Questions & Answers - IF Statements
sourceFile: IF Statements - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on if statements in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
25 % 25 is 0, and i = j assigns 0 to i. Convert.ToBoolean(0) is false, so the else branch runs, then "In main" is always printed.

Output:

In else
In main

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
Integer division is left-to-right: a / b * 2 is (32 / 8) * 2 = 8, so the if condition is never true. The else-if prints i while i != 4. When i is 4, break ends the loop.

Output:

0 1 2 3

questions.question: Which of the following conditions are true in the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Char.IsDigit('2') is true, so sample c is correct and d is not. Char.IsUpper('A') is true, so sample b is correct. Char.IsLower('a') is true, so sample a (which claims uppercase) is false. Only b and c are true.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Because WriteLine is used, each 0 or 1 is on its own line (and WriteLine("\n") adds a blank line after each row). The 1s form the anti-diagonal as i goes 2, 1, 0 and j goes 0, 1, 2: row i=2 is 0 0 1, row i=1 is 0 1 0, row i=0 is 1 0 0. Option c is that pattern. Console.ReadLine() inside the outer loop also pauses after each row.

questions.explanation: num is an array, so the element at i must be tested with num[i] % 2 == 0. Option a uses the array itself, option b is not an even/odd test, and option d uses assignment (=) instead of comparison (==).

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
Convert.ToBoolean(float) is true for any non-zero value. 0.002f - 0.1f is about -0.098f, so the first if is true and only "Sachin Tendulkar" is printed.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: Code execute successfully with no output

questions.explanation: a and b are variables, not constants. ++a is a value, not an assignable location, so ++a = ++b is illegal (CS0131: the left-hand side of an assignment must be a variable, property, or indexer).

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
0xB is hexadecimal 11. 022 is decimal 22 in C# (C# has no octal integer literals). '\xeb' is a hex char whose int value is 235. Convert.ToBoolean is false only for 0, so every if is true and "java" is printed. The dangling else ; statements are empty but legal.

Output:

java

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
|| short-circuits. ++a makes a = 6, which converts to true, so ++b is not evaluated and b stays 10. WriteLine prints a, a newline, then b.

Output:

6
10
